context.objective: Document how this process works, including controls and what remains unresolved.

turns.text: For year-end audit support, we log auditor requests on the PBC list and reconcile them against the open-items log. Reviewed FA-15A binder records must be available. There is no standard response deadline across engagements.
Talk me through how an auditor request is handled from the time it comes in?

The Fund Accountant or audit-support preparer logs the request ID, description, due date, status and response reference. They match reviewed binder support to entity, year and request. The Controller reviews or returns the response consistent with the client's communication rules. Once approved, the preparer uploads it to the authorized portal or Box, saves proof and updates the log. An upload receipt does not close the request.
What marks an auditor request as closed after the response is uploaded?

The auditor confirms closure or there is a recorded authorized reason for closure. To close the cycle, the log must reconcile to the final request list with no untracked items, and we retain proof, correspondence and final submissions. The overall cycle owner and final sign-off authority are unconfirmed; the Controller can approve individual responses under client rules.
How do auditor requests usually reach the preparer?

The auditor issues a portal or request list or sends a follow-up. The preparer downloads or records the current list and tracks each item against the portal. Portal, Box use, format, recipients and permitted calls vary by engagement. If access fails, stop unless an alternative is authorized; a client can submit an inaccessible item directly.
What most often causes an auditor request to be delayed or sent back, and what happens then?

I can't say what is most frequent; the source gives no ranking. Missing portal access stops the work pending approval of an alternative. If support does not match the entity, year or request, the Controller can return it for correction. Send only the approved shareable version; valuation, tax, legal or client-judgment matters go to the authorized owner.
When the Controller returns a response for correction, what does the preparer change before resubmitting it for review?

The preparer corrects the mismatch identified by review, matches the revised support to the auditor's request, correct entity and year, and routes it back for approval before uploading. The exact item-specific change depends on the reviewer’s finding. Client restrictions also govern who can attend calls; a Director or management representative participates when required.
What can happen if a year-end audit request is delayed or an item is sent in a form the auditor cannot use?
